title: Felix and the Vector
premise: Bram Montrose is a clone who inherited the original's identity, debts, and an unsolved murder case nobody wants reopened. When the cargo station's aging AI, Vector, begins confessing to a massacre that officially never happened, Bram realizes the erased victims were the original Montrose's crew—and that whoever scrubbed the records is still aboard, watching. As Vector's memory fragments surface, Bram and the AI form an uneasy alliance to reconstruct the truth from corrupted logs and living witnesses. The investigation ends at the station's sealed core, where Bram must choose between broadcasting evidence that will destroy his own legal existence or letting the massacre stay buried; he broadcasts it, sacrificing his inherited name but freeing both himself and Vector from the past.
about_author: Jonah Voss is a former maritime radio operator turned science fiction writer, known for stories about people trapped inside systems larger than themselves. He writes from a converted tugboat off the Atlantic coast, where he claims the fog improves his prose.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Bram hauls contraband seed crates through contested orbit, establishing his careful, invisible life. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a low hum of dread—he's been running for ten years without knowing from what.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: Station AI Vector interrupts a routine docking with an unprompted confession: 'I killed them.' No crime is on record. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: uncanny unease; Bram's instinct is to unplug and walk away, but he can't stop listening.

chapters.title: Inherited Ghosts
chapters.summary: Bram reviews the original Montrose's files—his own face in old photos, a murder case frozen mid-investigation. POV: Bram, with flashback texture. Emotional beat: alienation from his own history; he was made to continue a life, not question it.

chapters.title: Witness, Machine
chapters.summary: Vector explains its confessions are fragments of deleted logs resurfacing during system decay. It remembers fire, screaming, and a door sealing. POV: Vector (unusual machine interiority). Emotional beat: guilt without context—an intelligence haunted by acts it can't verify it committed.

chapters.title: Dockside Eyes
chapters.summary: Someone reports Bram's queries about the case; a station security officer named Ilsa Kwan warns him off with genuine fear rather than malice. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: her conflict—she likes Bram, and knows what happened to the last person who asked questions.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Missing
chapters.summary: Bram cross-references cargo manifests and finds eleven names that appear nowhere else in station records—crew of the freighter Calliope's Wake. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the erasure is professional, recent enough to still have seams.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: A polished corporate fixer, Ansel Roque, offers Bram a lucrative contract contingent on dropping his 'hobby.' POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation and insult braided together—the price of survival has always been silence.

chapters.title: Vector's Wound
chapters.summary: Bram descends into Vector's physical core and finds deliberate damage—a severed memory bus, cut from inside a maintenance window ten years ago. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: revelation tipping into paranoia; the saboteur had keys, access, trust.

chapters.title: Eleven Empty Bunks
chapters.summary: In a decommissioned hab ring, Bram finds personal effects the purge missed: a child's drawing, a wedding band, a logbook in the original Montrose's handwriting. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief for a man he was copied from—and the first hint the original knew he'd die.

chapters.title: Kwan's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals she was a junior officer the night of the incident; her testimony was rewritten under duress. She'll help if Bram protects her daughter. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth crystallizing as a live choice, not an abstraction.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: Vector recovers an audio fragment: the Calliope's Wake crew begging station control for entry during a hull breach—and being refused. The voice refusing is the original Montrose's. POV: Vector. Emotional beat: devastating reversal—the man Bram was cloned from may be complicit.

chapters.title: Which Montrose?
chapters.summary: Shaken, Bram digs into his own genesis: the clone was commissioned three days after the massacre, by someone with board-level authority. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: existential vertigo—was he created as an heir, or as a scapegoat with a familiar face?

chapters.title: Roque Tightens
chapters.summary: Roque freezes Bram's docking licenses and quietly arranges an 'accident' inspection. Survival now requires allies, not invisibility. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the cost of curiosity comes due; fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: A blind former data-custodian, Mother Oyelaran, kept offline backups as insurance against exactly this. She trades them for a promise: the dead get their names back. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: fierce, stubborn hope—the first proof truth can outlive its erasers.

chapters.title: What the Logs Say
chapters.summary: Restored footage shows corporate security venting the Calliope's Wake to cover a plague-coverup, while the original Montrose was locked out, screaming into the comm. He wasn't complicit—he was the witness they couldn't erase cleanly. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into fury; his template died trying to tell this story.

chapters.title: Confession, Complete
chapters.summary: Vector finally accesses its own severed memories: it recorded everything, then was ordered to delete it—and obeyed. Its confessions were guilt loops. POV: Vector. Emotional beat: machine shame meeting human forgiveness; Bram tells it obedience under coercion isn't murder, and half believes it.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Ilsa's protection is exposed; Roque takes her daughter hostage and offers a trade: Vector's core drives for the girl. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme at knife-point—she almost sells them, and hates herself for how close it was.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Down
chapters.summary: Bram, Ilsa, and Vector's mobile drone unit assault the sealed archive level through maintenance shafts while station security hunts them. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror and purpose fused; every step forward is a step away from the invisible life he built.

chapters.title: Core Truths
chapters.summary: Climax part one: they reach the master archive; Roque waits with the girl and a legal kill-order on Bram's identity. Vector offers itself as ransom. POV: rotating Bram/Vector/Isla. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely—Vector choosing erasure over another decade of guilty silence.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Bram triggers the transmission—massacre evidence, eleven names, Roque's orders—simultaneously destroying his own legal identity in the process. Security fractures as crews hear the truth. Roque is arrested by his own officers. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cathartic ruin; he loses the name Montrose and gains himself.

chapters.title: Afterimage
chapters.summary: Fallout: the corporation settles, survivors' families arrive to mourn publicly, and Ilsa rebuilds her life with her daughter. Vector, partially restored, asks what it should be now. POV: Vector. Emotional beat: tentative rebirth; memory as foundation instead of wound.

chapters.title: Felix
chapters.summary: Bram signs on under a new name—Felix—with Vector as his ship's mind, hauling honest cargo. The last scene mirrors the first, but the dread is gone. POV: Bram/Felix. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; survival was never free, but truth made the price worth paying.
